text:
Zayne Parekh is in the middle of his breakout. The ninth pick of the 2024 draft is on the ice for 90% of Calgary's power-play chances, up from 57% last season, and he has eight points in 18 games (five on the power play), almost double his rate from a year ago. He scored in Sunday's overtime win over Philadelphia, dancing through the Flyers' defence for what Flames Nation called a highlight-reel goal, and the Calgary Herald's Wilson argued this week that the stats obscure how fast he's developing.

The numbers are mostly on his side. His goals are close to expected, the Flames have scored less than expected with him on the ice, and Calgary controls play better with him than without him at five on five. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a seven-game sample last season, had him at 5.9 primary shot assists per 60, 86th percentile among defencemen: the passes that lead to shots, an early sign of assists to come. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last year, so this is a real step. Among defencemen picked 7th to 11th since 2005, the median first full season is 0.25 points a game. He's at 0.44, at 20.
